data.narrative:
Sila Nanotechnologies is a late-stage Climate & Energy company that has raised $1.3B+ to date. The comparable universe consists of 9 peers in the Climate & Energy sector: 1 public company (LNZA) and 8 private firms including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

The Stage-Progression method is the applicable triangulation approach here. Using total capital raised ($1.3B) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of Late Stage progression, this method implies a valuation of $1.6B. A Peer-Median approach was not viable; while 9 same-sector peers exist, no subset of 3+ companies met concurrent filters for stage, adjacent-stage proximity, and valuation-tier similarity, making a narrow peer multiple unreliable.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.3B (low) to $1.8B (median $1.6B). This range is anchored primarily to a single method, creating material methodological concentration risk. Key uncertainties include the absence of sufficient same-stage comparables to validate multiples independently, limiting the precision of any point estimate. A deeper valuation would benefit from access to recent transaction multiples or disclosed fundraising rounds among direct-stage peers in advanced materials and energy storage.
